2.name: text_block

0.name: block
0.value:
Turns a tensor of RATES into a tensor of random whole-number COUNTS:
each element is a Poisson sample whose average is the rate it holds.

Unlike t.dist.poisson, which uses one rate for every element, this node gives each element its own rate - the input IS the parameter. Feed it a picture of brightness and you get photon shot noise; feed it how busy each region should be and you get how many events each one gets this frame.

SYNTAX:
t.poisson
The node takes no arguments.

INPUTS and PARAMETERS:

tensor in:
The rates, one per element, each 0 or above (0 always gives 0). Every tensor that arrives is sampled and sent; this is the only inlet. A list or number is turned into a tensor first. If any value is negative the node sends NOTHING (and says why only with the app's verbose setting on). The tensor must be floating-point; an integer one gives an error in the console.

OUTPUTS:

tensor out:
Counts, the same shape, dtype and device as the input: whole numbers stored as floats (0.0, 1.0, 2.0 ...). A new draw every time a tensor arrives.

THE HISTOGRAM:
t.histc divides the range from its min to its max into equal bins and counts how many of the 4096 samples land in each; the bar plot draws the counts, the first bin at the left. Its shape is the shape of the distribution. Samples outside min..max are not counted at all.

READING THE DEMO:
Top: the rate slider sets t.full's value and clicks it, so a 64 x 64 tensor holding the SAME rate everywhere goes in. Its counts are the Poisson distribution itself: the heat_map (0 dark, 10 bright) is stepped speckle, and the histogram has one bar per count, 0 at the left to 20 at the right, peaking near the rate. Drag rate and the hump moves and widens.
Bottom: make_ramp sends rates rising from 0 at the left to top at the right (left heat_map), and the counts (right heat_map, same colours) are dark and sparse at the left and brighter and noisier to the right - each element drew from its own rate. Click 'again' for a fresh draw.

RELATED:
t.dist.poisson makes Poisson samples with one rate from a typed shape. t.bernoulli is the per-element yes/no version. t.geometric and t.exponential are other counts and waits.
